references.text: Just a few verses earlier, Jesus asks the blind man what he wants, and here He repeats the question directly: "What do you want me to do for you?" ([ref:Luk 18:36|Luke 18:36]). This shows Jesus' personal care by allowing the blind man himself to express his need.

In Mark's parallel account of the blind Bartimaeus, Jesus asks the same question: "What do you want me to do for you?", and Bartimaeus immediately answers with his wish to regain his sight ([ref:Mark 10:51|Mark 10:51]).
Matthew's parallel account of the two blind men at Jericho, where Jesus asks the same question and they answer: "Lord, let our eyes be opened" ([ref:Matt 20:32-33|Matthew 20:32-33]).
Another account where blind men call out to Jesus as "Son of David" and ask to regain their sight, and Jesus heals them according to their faith ([ref:Matt 9:27-29|Matthew 9:27-29]).

In the Nazareth synagogue, Jesus reads from Isaiah and declares that He is anointed to preach that the blind will receive sight ([ref:Luk 4:18|Luke 4:18]). The blind man's prayer to see is a direct fulfillment of this messianic mission.

Isaiah's prophecy about the messianic time: "Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened" ([ref:Jes 35:5|Isaiah 35:5]). The blind man's wish to regain his sight points toward this prophetic fulfillment.
The prophecy that Jesus quoted in Nazareth about the Lord's Spirit being upon Him to give sight to the blind ([ref:Jes 61:1-2|Isaiah 61:1-2]), which is made relevant by the blind man's prayer.

"The Lord opens the eyes of the blind" ([ref:Sal 146:8|Psalms 146:8]). The blind man's appeal to Jesus as "Lord" and his prayer to see reflect this psalm about God's power to open the eyes of the blind.
Jesus heals a man born blind in [ref:Joh 9:6-7|John 9:6-7], confirming Jesus' power over blindness and His role as the light of the world who gives sight to the blind.

Jesus' answer to the blind man's prayer comes immediately after: "Receive your sight! Your faith has saved you," and the man regained his sight and followed Jesus ([ref:Luk 18:42-43|Luke 18:42-43]). This shows that the man's faithful prayer was fully answered.
